clue.text: Mr. Mandragon, for one

parts.note: Mr Mandragon is the very rich man of a Hilaire Belloc cautionary verse, whose vast new house left him nowhere to live

explanation.surface: A character from comic verse is offered as a type.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc's poem about Mr Mandragon names him in its title by his wealth; the clue asks for that label.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Mandragon is an example of a person whose fortune runs to seven figures or more.

clue.text: Supplied by Slough Heat & Light Co.?

definitions.text: Supplied by Slough Heat & Light Co.?

parts.words: Supplied by Slough Heat & Light Co.?
parts.note: a slough is a bog, so a utility company of the swamp would pipe out the fuel that rises from rotting vegetation there

explanation.surface: A bill from the gas and electricity company in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here 'slough' is a common noun meaning a bog; methane bubbling from bogs is the product.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the gas given off by decaying plants in wet, boggy ground.

clue.text: Doncaster race tomorrow at Auteuil? Tricky

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun meaning trickery

parts.note: the St Leger is the classic horse race run at Doncaster
Auteuil is a Paris racecourse, and the French word for tomorrow is demain

explanation.surface: A racing tipster pairs today's Doncaster race with tomorrow's in Paris and finds it hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger, run at Doncaster in England, gives LEGER; Auteuil, a Paris racecourse, points to French. The definition 'Tricky' is looser than modern practice, an adjective for the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is a tricky business, so the old word for conjuring trickery is described by the adjective.

clue.text: In the act, he escapes. Nothing tampered with

indicators.note: when he escapes, the letters of that word get out of the phrase before it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thief caught red-handed slips away, though nothing was disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escapes' takes HE out of INTHEACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged has had nothing tampered with.

clue.text: When the headless man in armour appears

indicators.note: a headless figure has lost the top, so the word for him drops its first letter

parts.note: a knight is a man in armour

explanation.surface: Ghost-story lore: a headless knight walks after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' strips the K from KNIGHT. The surface suggests a ghost, which is apt, since the definition 'When' points to the hours of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness is the time when ghosts walk, so it answers the question 'when?'.

clue.text: Stupid-he or we?

parts.note: the word is a dull fellow in English and, in Latin, means 'we do not know', so it describes a stupid he or a confused we

explanation.surface: A grumble about who is the fool: him, or all of us?
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin verb form means 'we do not know', which is how the English noun for a know-nothing came about.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-nothing is a stupid person, and the Latin original is first person plural: we are ignorant.

clue.text: The police in the end conscripted?

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of the other, splitting it

parts.note: taken as written
the police are the force

explanation.surface: In the end, were the police called up for military service?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The police' is a stock phrase for the force; the question mark flags that conscription is not usually done by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscripted service is compelled, imposed on people by law.

clue.text: This, in short, for a digest

definitions.text: This, in short, for a digest

parts.words: This, in short, for a digest
parts.note: the organ that digests food has a short, childish name, a clipped form of tummy

explanation.surface: A summary is offered in brief for a magazine digest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digest' is a verb's worth of work here: the thing that digests, i.e. the stomach, in short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipped colloquial word for the stomach, the organ of digestion.

clue.text: Drive from here to 7 across develops top-spin

definitions.text: Drive from here to 7 across develops top-spin

parts.words: Drive from here to 7 across develops top-spin
parts.note: a golfer drives from a raised peg; that word, then 'to', then the 7-across light makes the name of a small spinning top

explanation.surface: Golf coaching: a drive struck from here puts topspin on the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A teetotum is a small top spun with the fingers; the clue builds it from this answer, 'to' and 7 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer drives off from the small peg, or the patch of ground it stands on.

clue.text: It is sung in a remote temple

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words a remote temple

explanation.surface: Chanting heard in a distant shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters inside 'remote temple'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short polyphonic choral piece with sacred words is a song for voices.

clue.text: Off-side but O.K.

definitions.meaning: the off side of a horse or vehicle is its ...-hand side

explanation.definitionFit: The off side of a car or horse is the right one, and something correct or satisfactory is all right.

clue.text: Put your cap on the floor

definitions.text: Put your cap on the floor

parts.words: Put your cap on the floor
parts.note: the cap is a kneecap; putting it to the ground is bending the knee in reverence

explanation.surface: An instruction to doff your hat and drop it on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cap' suggests a hat, but it is the kneecap.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneel briefly in worship lowers the knee, and so the kneecap, to the ground.

clue.text: What a stew you're in, old bean!

definitions.meaning: a ragout of mutton and vegetables goes by this name
the white kidney bean has the same name

explanation.surface: A friendly 'old bean' is told he is in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' is a fix, and 'old bean' is dated British slang for a chum; both conceal food senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a French mutton ragout and the small white kidney bean.

clue.text: Dish in "Going for a Song " ?

parts.note: something going for a song is a cheap find, a ... of luck, and split differently that phrase is a savoury toasted-cheese dish

explanation.surface: A dish featured in a show or song called Going for a Song.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's two halves apart: a rare bit of bargain, as when goods go for a song. Welsh rarebit is cheese melted on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a dish of melted cheese on toast.

clue.text: One town being the founder of another!

parts.note: basing something is founding it, acting as its founder
another town: Stoke, the Staffordshire pottery town

explanation.surface: A claim that one English town founded a second.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke-on-Trent is a pottery town in the English Midlands; Basingstoke is a Hampshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Basingstoke is a town in Hampshire, southern England.

clue.text: Topping simian kiss

parts.note: a simian is an ape
a kiss is written as X at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A rave about a marvellous monkey kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' reads as old British slang for excellent, but it is the noun: the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or summit of something tops it off.

clue.text: No joinery, no coal-mining

definitions.meaning: work with no joins has no seams
coal lies in seams, so with none there is no mining

explanation.definitionFit: Without joins in the work, and without any coal beds to dig.

clue.text: Can the soul of France rise above race? That is the issue

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed above another comes first
in a down light a word that rises is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the French word for soul is âme
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about French spirit and racial pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns AME into EMA, and 'above' puts it over NATION in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that flows out of a source is an issue from it.

clue.text: Catching a girl before she can begin going

definitions.text: Catching a girl before she can begin going

parts.words: Catching a girl before she can begin going
parts.note: roping with a noose is pictured as roping a lass, stopping a young woman before she gets away

explanation.surface: A suitor grabs his sweetheart before she can leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's start sounds out a lass, the Scots and northern word for girl, being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching an animal with a noosed rope thrown from a distance.

clue.text: Atlantis?

parts.note: the legendary island that sank under the sea, the main, was land in the main

explanation.surface: A one-word question about the lost island of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is an old word for the open sea, so Atlantis, now under the sea, is land of the main.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent proper, as opposed to islands, is the land Atlantis is set against.

clue.text: Ena taps a foot

annotationWithheld.why: 'Ena taps a foot' is an anagram of ENA TAPS A defined by 'foot' with no anagram indicator: 'taps' would have to be both fodder and indicator

clue.text: She would have made a poor match for a nabob

definitions.text: She would have made a poor match for a nabob

parts.words: She would have made a poor match for a nabob
parts.note: a nabob is a rich man back from India; this girl's name is also a small old Indian coin, a poor match, and like the word nabob it reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A gossip judges a woman an unsuitable bride for a wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: A nabob was a man who made a fortune in India; the name doubles as a coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name that is also a small copper Indian coin, poor beside a nabob's wealth.

clue.text: The home Prior made?

parts.note: read Prior as prior: a home made beforehand, built in a factory and assembled on site

explanation.surface: Asks about the house built by Prior, perhaps the poet Matthew Prior.
explanation.walkthrough: Postwar Britain built many factory-made temporary houses with this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory-built house put up quickly on site from ready-made sections.

clue.text: Cadenus's beautiful bluestocking

parts.note: Swift's poem pairs Cadenus, Swift himself, with the clever young woman Esther Vanhomrigh under a coined name

explanation.surface: A literary allusion to a learned woman admired by Swift's alter ego.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift's poem 'Cadenus and Vanessa' gives the name; Cadenus is an anagram of decanus, dean.
explanation.definitionFit: The coined name Swift gave Esther Vanhomrigh, an educated woman he tutored.

clue.text: Striking for six and sixpence

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
VI for six plus d, the old British abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Workers go on strike for a wage of six shillings and sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: In pre-decimal British money d stood for pence, so sixpence is VI D.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright and arresting, as a colour or image is.

clue.text: Burns's maiden starts with a prayer

definitions.text: Burns's maiden starts with a prayer

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
an orison is a prayer

explanation.surface: A poet's sweetheart begins her day on her knees.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns wrote the song 'Mary Morison'; her surname is M followed by a word for a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Morison is the girl in a Burns love song.

clue.text: Cloven head versus cloven hoof, as it were

definitions.text: Cloven head versus cloven hoof, as it were

parts.words: Cloven head versus cloven hoof, as it were
parts.note: a bishop's tall headdress is split at the top, set against the devil's split foot, church versus evil

explanation.surface: A contest between a creature with a split skull and one with split feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The devil is pictured with cloven hooves; the bishop opposes him wearing a cloven hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall headdress, which has a cleft top.

clue.text: Cat as witness of neat moon orbit?

definitions.text: Cat as witness of neat moon orbit?

parts.words: Cat as witness of neat moon orbit?
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the cat plays the fiddle as the cow, neat being old word for cattle, jumps over the moon

explanation.surface: A cat watches a tidy lunar orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is not tidy but an old word for cattle; the rhyme is 'Hey diddle diddle, the cat and the fiddle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat in the rhyme plays the fiddle, so it is a performer on that instrument.

clue.text: "A series of masses and fugues and ." (Gilbert)

definitions.text: "A series of masses and fugues and ." (Gilbert)

parts.words: "A series of masses and fugues and ." (Gilbert)
parts.note: the Mikado's punishment for a music-hall singer ends with a word for musical works, in Cockney form

explanation.surface: Fill the blank in a line from W S Gilbert.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Mikado the music-hall singer must hear 'masses and fugues and ‘ops’ by Bach'; the word is a dropped-h opus plural and pun on hops.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for opuses, numbered musical works, completing Gilbert's line.

clue.text: Sharp girl William was

parts.note: the Scottish writer William Sharp published as a woman, Macleod, under a girl's first name

explanation.surface: A remark that clever little William was really a sharp girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks like an adjective but is William Sharp's surname; he wrote Celtic romances as a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The female first name William Sharp wrote under.

clue.text: Temper sends him up the wall

definitions.text: Temper sends him up the wall

parts.words: Temper sends him up the wall
parts.note: the classical underworld god's name, put before temper, makes a paint applied to walls

explanation.surface: Someone's bad temper drives him mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Distemper is a water-based wall paint; the god of the underworld Dis plus 'temper' builds it, so temper sends him up the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is the Roman name for Pluto, ruler of the underworld.

clue.text: One of those gilts for which there was a fair demand

definitions.text: One of those gilts for which there was a fair demand

parts.words: One of those gilts for which there was a fair demand
parts.note: gilts are government bonds, but here the gilt is gold leaf on spiced cake, sold at country fairs

explanation.surface: Financial news: one gilt-edged stock in steady demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the gilt on the gingerbread' is an idiom; such cakes were gilded and sold at fairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilded spiced cake was a traditional treat sold at fairs.
